affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It costs the police two units and their authority over the case, and it ends any chance of taking Trinity by conventional means — the ordinary world's tools are shown to be useless against her.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The scene nodes give no off-screen reaction beyond the on-screen participants; the Agents' takeover is shown directly, not reacted to from elsewhere.

events.summary: Trinity's planned exit collapses when Morpheus tells her the hardline is cut and Agents are in the building, so she is redirected to a phone at Wells and Lake and forced to run for it. She breaks through the hall past Agent Brown, climbs the fire escape when Smith blocks the alley, and crosses the rooftops with impossible leaps that the cops cannot match but that Brown duplicates. events.title: The Agents seize Neo at the office
events.summary: A cell phone delivered to Neo's cubicle connects him to Morpheus, who warns that the Agents are coming and guides him through the office as a search closes in. Neo slips past the search and into an empty office, where Morpheus directs him to a scaffold and window as the only exit. He climbs back inside just as a cop reaches the room, and is taken: the Agents lead him handcuffed
events.action: The event opens with Neo at his cubicle receiving a phone that rings with Morpheus on the line, warning that the Agents are coming and that he does not know what they will do. Neo glimpses Agent Smith, Agent Brown and Agent Jones leading cops onto the floor, and a female employee points out his cubicle. Following Morpheus's turn-by-turn commands, Neo lunges into an empty cubicle, hides while the Agents search his own, then rolls out, freezes behind a cop, and sneaks across the row into an empty office. There Morpheus directs him to open a window and cross a scaffold to the roof; Neo refuses, then relents and climbs onto the ledge, but a blast of wind knocks him off balance, he drops the phone, and he retreats inside just as a cop opens the door. The Agents then lead a handcuffed Neo out of the skyscraper and force him into a dark sedan, while Trinity watches the capture in her motorcycle's rearview mirror and curses.

As the pressure gauge climbs and the ultrasound monitor shows the bug slithering beneath his skin, Switch warns it is on the move and about to be lost. Trinity refuses, fires an electric charge into Neo, and convulses a fluke-like bug out through the extractor's coils; she lifts the glass cage showing it squirming, then rolls down the window and dumps it onto the pavement, where it reverts to a common wire tap. The car then disappears into the rainy night and stops in a deserted alley behind Hotel Lafayette.

events.title: The Red Pill
events.summary: Trinity delivers Neo to Morpheus at Hotel Lafayette room 1313, then Morpheus converts Neo's lifelong nameless dread into a named enemy and an irreversible, self-chosen commitment before the crew's trace program unmans him physically. Neo swallows the red pill and is then wired into a chair where a cracking mirror liquefies, crawls up his body, and drives him into cardiac arrest just as the crew locks his location and Morpheus sends the signal that swallows him into darkness.
events.action: Trinity leads Neo to room 1313 and warns him to be honest because 'He knows more than you can possibly imagine.' Morpheus receives Neo in the adjacent room, reframes his hacker worship into a felt conviction that something is wrong with the world, defines the Matrix as an enslaving illusion no one can be told about, and offers the choice of two pills. Neo swallows the red pill. In the equipment room, Trinity fixes electrode disks to Neo while Morpheus explains the pill is a trace program to pinpoint his location; the cracked mirror heals into liquid, invades Neo's body, and triggers fibrillation and arrest. Apoc secures the lock and Morpheus orders Tank to send the signal, and Neo is pulled screaming into darkness.

events.title: Born Into the Real World
events.summary: Neo tears free of his pod in a vast human power plant, is disconnected by a machine and sucked into a black hole, flushed through waste lines and a sewer main, then hauled aboard a hovercraft where Morpheus greets him by name before he blacks out.
events.action: Neo ruptures the gelatin shroud of his pod and stands, bald and naked, able to breathe for the first time. He finds a coaxial cable locked into the base of his skull and looks out over endless rows of pods holding motionless human beings, each a glowing petal on a tower spiraling to incomprehensible heights. A machine seizes him, opens the cable lock, slides a needle and cerebrum-chip from his skull, and a vacuum sucks him and the gelatin into a black hole. He falls and slides through a waste line, is flushed up through grease traps, and begins to drown in the sewer main before a metallic cable snatches him into a flying machine. Aboard a hovercraft, a metal harness drops him half-conscious to the floor; human hands and arms help him up until he is looking straight at Morpheus, who smiles and welcomes him to the real world, and then Neo passes out.

events.title: Waking and Rebuilding
events.summary: Neo surfaces from the rescue into a hovercraft infirmary where Morpheus and Dozer rebuild his wasted body, then into his own room where Morpheus replaces explanation with a single temporal blow—the year is near 2197—and leads him out to be shown the truth rather than told it.
events.action: Morpheus reports to Trinity that the search found 'him,' answers her doubt with certainty, and then steadies the waking Neo with small doses of truth while Dozer repairs his atrophied muscles; once Neo is rebuilt, Morpheus reframes Neo's questions from 'what' to 'when,' delivers the loss of two centuries, and converts teaching into a visual demonstration, guiding Neo up toward the main deck.

state_triples.reading: Morpheus treats certainty as a discipline he imposes on the room: he corrects Trinity's 'hope' with 'know,' then repeats the same withholding toward Neo, doling out just enough truth to keep the body calm and deferring the rest. His gentleness and his refusal to explain are the same gesture—he is protecting a conviction he held before Neo could speak for himself, and steering a man he already believes is 'the one' toward a revelation he is confident will land.

Trinity refuses to let triumph close the moment, naming the risk that they may have gotten it wrong; her 'I hope you're right' is the counterweight Morpheus feels compelled to correct, and her staying off-page keeps her emotionally at a distance from the reverent framing he gives the rescue.
